questions.question: Fill in blank (A) with the most appropriate preposition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**with**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The sentence describes **India** as a country that possesses a diverse and rich heritage. 
• The preposition '**with**' is used to indicate having or possessing a particular quality, feature, or characteristic. 
• In the context of the phrase 'a nation **with** a rich cultural, scientific, and historical legacy', it correctly identifies the attributes associated with **India**. 
• Other prepositions like '**in**', '**of**', or '**by**' do not correctly establish the relationship of possession or descriptive characteristic in this grammatical structure. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'. Complete Passage: ***India**, as a nation 1. **with**__ a rich cultural, scientific, and historical legacy, confers several prestigious awards to honour extraordinary achievements and contributions across different fields. Among these, the highest-ranking awards 2. __**hold**__ special significance, as they represent the nation's deepest gratitude and recognition of excellence. At the pinnacle of civilian honours stands the **Bharat Ratna**, instituted in **1954**. It is the highest civilian award of **India**, awarded for exceptional service in art, literature, science, and public service of the highest order. Over the years, eminent personalities like **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar**, **Lata Mangeshkar**, and **Sachin Tendulkar** have been recipients of this rare honour. In the realm of 3. __**gallantry**__, the **Param Vir Chakra (PVC)** is the nation's most distinguished military award. It is presented for acts of 4. __**conspicuous**__ bravery and supreme sacrifice in the presence of the enemy. Brave soldiers like **Major Somnath Sharma** and **Captain Vikram Batra** have been decorated with this honour, symbolizing courage and patriotism at its peak. In addition, **India** also recognizes valour through other gallantry awards like the **Ashoka Chakra**, the highest peacetime bravery award. For contributions in civilian life, the **Padma Awards**, **Padma Vibhushan**, **Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Shri** acknowledge distinguished service in varied disciplines. These awards not only celebrate individual achievements but also 5. __**inspire**__ generations by highlighting the values of dedication, courage, and service to the nation. They embody **India**'s respect for those who go beyond personal ambition to contribute to society and the country's progress.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **In**: Generally used to indicate a location, a period of time, or being inside something. 
• **Of**: Often used to show belonging, origin, or what something is made of. 
• **By**: Usually indicates the means, the agent performing an action, or proximity. </ul

questions.question: Choose the correct option to fill in blank (A).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**was filled**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The passage begins with the time marker '**Last month**', which establishes that the entire narrative is set in the **past tense**. 
• Supporting verbs in the context, such as '**went**' and '**started**', further confirm that the actions occurred in the past. 
• '**Was filled**' is the **Simple Past Passive** form, which is used to describe the state or condition of the atmosphere at that specific time. 
• The other options are incorrect because: 
• '**Fills**' is in the **Simple Present** tense, used for habits or general facts. 
• '**Will fill**' is in the **Future** tense. 
• '**Has filled**' is in the **Present Perfect** tense, which implies a connection to the present. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'. Complete Passage: *Last month, our class went on an excursion to the National Science Museum. The atmosphere 1. **was filled**__ with excitement as the bus started its journey. Our teacher reminded us to observe carefully and note important details, because the trip was meant to combine fun with learning. As we entered the museum, we saw fascinating models of satellites, robots, and ancient tools. One section 2. __**displayed**__ the history of Indian inventions, from the concept of zero to modern space missions. Everyone listened attentively to the guide, who explained each exhibit with clarity. During the break, a friend said, 'Without science, progress would have been impossible.' Another replied, 'True, but blind dependence on machines 3. __**may**__ lead us into laziness and health problems.' Their discussion showed how science could inspire both admiration and caution. In the afternoon, we attended a workshop on renewable energy. The instructor emphasized that innovation must go hand in hand with responsibility. His words 4. __**served as**__ a reminder that every discovery has consequences, good or bad. On our way back, the teacher concluded, 'The museum visit has not just enriched your knowledge but also encouraged you to think critically. 5. __**Curiosity**__ and responsibility are the pillars of education.'* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• The **Passive Voice** (was/were + V3) is often used when the focus is on the state or the recipient of the action rather than the performer. In this case, the focus is on the **atmosphere** being characterized by **excitement**. </ul

• The verbs used throughout the narrative, such as '**went**', '**started**', '**entered**', and '**saw**', are all in the **simple past tense**. 
• Blank (B) requires a verb to describe what the museum section showed during the visit. To maintain **tense consistency**, the past tense form '**displayed**' must be used. 
• Other options like '**display**' (present plural), '**displays**' (present singular), and '**will display**' (future) do not fit the chronological context of the story. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'. Complete Passage: *Last month, our class went on an excursion to the National Science Museum. • **Simple Past Tense** is used to describe completed actions that happened at a specific time in the past. 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement**: Since '**One section**' is a singular subject, if the sentence were in the present tense, '**displays**' would be used; however, the past tense remains '**displayed**' regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural (for most verbs). </ul

questions.question: Which of the following modal verbs correctly fills in blank (C) and completes the sentence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**may**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The sentence is expressing a **possibility** or a **potential consequence** regarding the over-reliance on technology. 
• The modal verb '**may**' is used to indicate that something is possible, even if it is not certain. In this context, it suggests that blind dependence on machines has the potential to lead to laziness and health issues. 
• '**Would**' is typically used for **hypothetical** or **conditional** situations, which is less appropriate here as the speaker is talking about a realistic risk. 
• '**Will**' indicates **certainty** or a definite future outcome, which might be too absolute for a cautionary opinion. 
• '**Shal**' is a misspelling of '**shall**' and is generally used with the first person (I/We) for suggestions or formal future statements. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'. Complete Passage: *Last month, our class went on an excursion to the National Science Museum. The atmosphere **was filled**__ with excitement as the bus started its journey. Our teacher reminded us to observe carefully and note important details, because the trip was meant to combine fun with learning. As we entered the museum, we saw fascinating models of satellites, robots, and ancient tools. One section __**displayed**__ the history of Indian inventions, from the concept of zero to modern space missions. Everyone listened attentively to the guide, who explained each exhibit with clarity. During the break, a friend said, ‘Without science, progress would have been impossible.’ Another replied, ‘True, but blind dependence on machines __**may**__ lead us into laziness and health problems.’ Their discussion showed how science could inspire both admiration and caution. In the afternoon, we attended a workshop on renewable energy. The instructor emphasized that innovation must go hand in hand with responsibility. His words __**served as**__ a reminder that every discovery has consequences, good or bad. On our way back, the teacher concluded, ‘The museum visit has not just enriched your knowledge but also encouraged you to think critically. __**Curiosity**__ and responsibility are the pillars of education.’* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Possibility (May/Might/Can)**: Used to express that something could happen. '**May**' is more formal and indicates a medium level of probability. 
• **Necessity/Certainty (Must/Will)**: Used when there is no doubt about the outcome or when something is required. 
• **Hypothetical (Would)**: Used when talking about imaginary or conditional scenarios.
